limits.reference: SourceAssets/characters-review/PilgrimRigV2/PilgrimRigV2.glb (the file the V2 residents were imported from), cross-checked against rig-definition.json
limits.nativeGate: Before the skeletal batch is saved: bone names in authored order, rest positions within 0.05 cm of the Interchange frame (x, -y, z), skeleton created inside the variant folder, four clips on that skeleton, each clip rotation-only except pelvis (AnimationLibrary.get_bone_poses_for_frame vs AnimPose reference). Any unavailable API blocks the save; it never assumes.
limits.honestCeiling: Whole-arm A-pose direction drifts 0.12 deg; the individual elbow/wrist/toe rest directions move 4.96/4.32/3.81 deg because the segments were lengthened. Rotation curves ride on those rest offsets, so V3 poses differ from V2 exactly by the proportion change. Hand and foot contact still need PIE eyes.

scope: Byte-level proof on the delivered GLBs against the delivered V2 GLB. It proves the V2 motion (rotation curves plus pelvis translation) is well-defined on every V3 skeleton. It is not the native Skeleton identity: Interchange creates one Skeleton per variant and the base readback re-proves names/rest pose/clips natively before save.
honestCeiling: Segment-level rest directions did move (elbow ~4.96 deg, wrist ~4.32 deg, toe ~3.81 deg) because arm and foot were lengthened; the whole-arm A-pose direction moved 0.12 deg. Rotation curves apply on top of these rest offsets, so poses differ from V2 by exactly the proportion change and by nothing else. Visible hand/foot contact still needs PIE eyes.
